definitions.explanation: The gathering of crops; the crops that are gathered.
Something valuable obtained from an effort or experience.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}は{収穫|しゅうかく}の{季節|きせつ}だ。
{今年|ことし}は{米|こめ}の{収穫|しゅうかく}が{多|おお}かった。
examples.english: This year's rice harvest was plentiful.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{研修|けんしゅう}は{大|おお}きな{収穫|しゅうかく}があった。{新|あたら}しい{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{学|まな}んだだけでなく、{世界|せかい}{各国|かっこく}の{同僚|どうりょう}と{知|し}り{合|あ}うことができた。
examples.english: The overseas training was very fruitful. Not only did I learn new techniques, but I was also able to meet colleagues from around the world.
examples.notes: 収穫 used figuratively for 'gains/fruits of effort'

notes:
{収穫|しゅうかく} means harvest (literal) or gains/fruits of effort (figurative).

LITERAL USAGE:
- {収穫|しゅうかく}する (to harvest)
- {収穫|しゅうかく}{期|き} (harvest season)
- {収穫|しゅうかく}{量|りょう} (harvest yield)
- {収穫|しゅうかく}{祭|さい} (harvest festival)

FIGURATIVE USAGE:
- {大|おお}きな{収穫|しゅうかく}があった (there were great gains)
- {収穫|しゅうかく}の{多|おお}い{旅|たび} (a trip with many rewards)

RELATED TERMS:
- {収穫|しゅうかく}: harvest (general term)
- {稲刈|いねか}り: rice harvesting
- {実|みの}り: fruition, harvest (also figurative)
